findings.title: Tokenizer furigana teaches wrong readings in flagship texts (神→しん in deity names, 都→と in 野ばら)
findings.evidence: The reader renders precomputed tokenizer readings as furigana (rubySource:'tokenizer' on 60/70 curated articles), and they are wrong on content words in exactly the texts a learner opens first. (1) 検収前 original 造化三神に出会う朝 (bunki-graded-n3-zoka-sanjin-morning.json): tokens 32/40/43/102/118/121 give 神 the reading しん inside deity names — 天之御中主神 renders as ruby あめのみなかぬし+神(しん), correct reading かみ; the SAME file has 神=かみ at token 114, so the article teaches two readings for the same word in the same names. Rendered in DOM: body text '高天原たかまがはらに天之御中主あめのみなかぬしの | 神しん'. (2) Aozora 野ばら (aozora:051034): token 42 gives 都 the reading と in ここは都から遠い — correct みやこ; ruby renders 都(と) on tap and in つねに mode. (3) wikinews-1403: 14日 splits to 14+日(か), so the ladder shows 日=か mid-date. Furigana is the corridor's core teaching surface; a demanding learner taking these readings at face value learns them wrong, and nothing in the UI marks tokenizer readings as unverified (the 検収前 flag covers editorial acceptance, not per-token reading confidence).
findings.repro: Serve prototypes/corridor, 390x844. Shelf → open 造化三神に出会う朝 → tap 神 after 天之御中主 → furigana しん appears (or set ふりがな=つねに and read the first paragraph). Shelf → 野ばら → set ふりがな=つねに → third sentence shows 都(と). Data check: python3 -c on the two article JSONs, tokens listed above.

findings.title: Back from an archive article dumps you at the wrong scroll position in the year list — place lost among 93 rows
findings.evidence: back() for a reader whose passage file starts with 'archive/' does S.view='archive'; render(); return; with no scroll save or restore (corridor.js:2201-2205 — contrast the very next branch, which restores S.shelfScroll for the shelf). No archiveScroll is ever recorded anywhere (grep: only shelfScroll/readerScroll/readerPos exist). Measured live: expanded 2016 (93 rows), scrolled to row 40 (window.scrollY 4570), opened it, tapped 戻る → returned to the archive at scrollY 2305 — the February rows, ~2270px above the row just read (screenshot 21-back-to-archive.png; the opened 2016-07-11 row is far below the fold). A learner reading a year chronologically must re-find their place after every article; the 読了 ✓ marks help only after re-scrolling. The year's expanded state is kept (S.archiveYears), which makes the missing scroll restore the one broken leg.
findings.repro: Shelf → 新聞アーカイブ → expand 2016年 → scroll ~4500px down → open any row → 戻る. Land ~2300px, not where you were.
findings.anchors: prototypes/corridor/corridor.js:2201-2205 (no scrollTo on the archive return), 2093-2100 (keepScroll handles only reader/shelf); screenshots 19-archive-2016.png, 21-back-to-archive.png

findings.title: Difficulty subtitle '~1 in 2 words beyond the JLPT lists' is near-constant and contradicts the level pill — a Beginner one-liner claims half its words are beyond JLPT
findings.evidence: levelPhrase (corridor.js:36-63) floors the vocab note at oneIn=Math.max(2,…), and the jlpt_lexicon coverage in the shipped grading data is ~0.5-0.67 for nearly everything, so 68 of the 69 graded shelf cards read '~1 in 2' or '~1 in 3 words beyond the JLPT lists' — identical wording from 初級前半 to 上級後半 (data census: {2:38, 3:29, 4:2, 5:1}). Live DOM: the やさしい日本語 glossary card 育児休業給付金 shows 'Beginner | 初級前半 · ~1 in 2 words beyond the JLPT lists' — a Beginner-graded single sentence of basic administrative Japanese asserting every other word is beyond ALL JLPT lists, directly beside the Beginner pill. As a signal it discriminates nothing (a learner comparing cards to pick a readable text gets the same number on almost every card) and as a claim it reads as self-contradictory, undermining trust in the grading pills.
findings.repro: Load ?entry=shelf, scroll the 70 cards: the vocab note is '1 in 2' or '1 in 3' on all but one. Find 育児休業給付金 for the Beginner contradiction. Census: parse grading.signals.jlpt_lexicon.coverage across data/articles/index.json.
findings.anchors: prototypes/corridor/corridor.js:50-61 (Math.max(2,…) floor, jlpt fallback wording); prototypes/corridor/data/articles/index.json grading signals; screenshot 01-shelf-top.png

findings.title: Galaxy nav-search session is razed by coming back from a result: query, results and focus all gone
findings.evidence: Driven live (playwright + system chromium, 390x844 touch). Open ginga nav, type 水 (8 result rows render), tap the first row -> word sheet opens over the drift (crumb 'galaxy › 水', focus on sheet-back). Tap sheet-back (or Escape): state returns to ginga home with navOpen=false, #nav-search-input no longer exists (value null), 0 result rows, and document.activeElement falls to <body>. A learner comparing several hits must re-open the nav and retype the query for every single result. Mechanism: the result-row click handler sets S.navOpen=false before go() (corridor.js:11289), buildNavSearch keeps the query only in the transient input node (never in S), and restoreDialogInvoker cannot refocus a .nav-search-row that was destroyed with the bar. Screenshots 03-search.png, 04-after-result.png, 06-after-sheet-back.png in scratchpad/hunt. Contrast: the shelf's search keeps S.query (corridor.js:2600-2622) and survives the same round trip.
findings.repro: 1) Serve prototypes/corridor, open / (galaxy home). 2) Tap #ginga-symbol, type 水 into #nav-search-input. 3) Tap the first .nav-search-row (sheet opens). 4) Tap #sheet-back. Observe: nav closed, query and results gone, focus on body.
findings.anchors: prototypes/corridor/corridor.js:11289 (row click sets S.navOpen=false), 11256-11320 (query lives only in the DOM input), 11441-11442 (heroMode re-render), 2073-2088 (restoreDialogInvoker has nothing to restore)

findings.title: Archive room restores no scroll context in either direction: back to shelf lands ~20,000px from the archive door; back from an archive article lands at the reader's scroll, not the list's
findings.evidence: Driven live. (a) The archive door sits at the bottom of the 70-article shelf (window.scrollY 20882 when it is centered). Enter archive, scroll the year list to 571, press back: view=shelf but scrollY stays 571 — the learner is dumped near the top of the shelf, ~20,300px from where they were. The back() archive branch (corridor.js:2181-2185) is missing the window.scrollTo(0, S.shelfScroll) that the sibling reader/tray branch performs at 2206. (b) Expand a year, scroll list to 800, open an archive article, scroll the article to 1200, press back: view=archive but scrollY stays 1200 — an arbitrary spot set by how far you read, not the list position. Structural cause: keepScroll/returnScroll only know 'reader' and 'shelf' (corridor.js:2092-2101); no archive scroll memory exists at all. Minor rider: the archive reader's crumb reads 'bookshelf › <title>', dropping the archive ancestor. Screenshots 40-back-archive.png, 41-back-shelf.png, 42-back-archive2.png.
findings.repro: Serve corridor, open /?entry=shelf. scrollIntoView #archive-link (note window.scrollY ≈ 20880), click it. Scroll archive to 571, click #back -> shelf at 571. Re-enter, expand a year, scroll to 800, open an .archive-row, scroll article to 1200, click #back -> archive at 1200.
findings.anchors: prototypes/corridor/corridor.js:2181-2185 (archive->shelf branch, no scrollTo), 2201-2205 (archive-reader->archive branch, no scroll restore), 2092-2101 (keepScroll/returnScroll know only reader+shelf), 2815-2819 (archive-link click)

findings.title: Keyboard-only learner at the galaxy home: first Tab lands on an invisible button, and no galaxy word is reachable at all
findings.evidence: Driven live. At the drift home the Tab cycle is: radocX -> ginga-symbol -> ginga-theme-seal -> body -> (repeat). radocX is the 閉じる × close button of the drift layer's radicals explainer (#radoc), which at rest is opacity:0 + pointer-events:none (drift-layer.css:169-173) — invisible, yet its button stays in the tab order and takes focus (drift-layer.js:8 injects it; nothing sets tabindex=-1 or hidden while closed). Meanwhile the 80 word nodes in #sky have tabIndex -1 / are plain DIVs (evaluate: 80 sky children, 0 tabbable), so the three-stage tap ladder (furigana -> gloss -> dive), the bloom, the card and its study door are all pointer-only — a keyboard user can only leave the galaxy via the chrome (shelf/tutor/dojo). Also, Escape does not close the open ginga nav bar (no keydown handler covers S.navOpen; only sheets at corridor.js:10482, the stroke room at 10227 and the world picker at 11125 handle Escape) — closable by keyboard only by tabbing back to #ginga-symbol and pressing Enter (verified working).
findings.repro: Open / (galaxy). Press Tab once: activeElement is #radocX inside the fully transparent #radoc overlay. Keep tabbing: no word in #sky is ever reached. Open the nav with Enter on #ginga-symbol, press Escape: gingaOpen stays true.
findings.anchors: prototypes/corridor/drift-layer.js:8 (radoc markup incl. radocX), drift-layer.css:169-173 (opacity:0/pointer-events:none, button left focusable), drift-layer.js:2053 (Escape only closes radoc); corridor.js word nodes: renderEntry field words and drift sky words carry no tabindex

findings.title: Device/browser Back anywhere except the writing room exits the SPA and razes all navigation context (sheet stack, dive, room)
findings.evidence: Driven live. The stroke room's history sentinel works exactly as designed: with the quiet stroke page open, history.state carries bunkiStrokeRoom{token,id,sheetScroll,invoker}, and history.back() closes ONLY the stroke page, restoring the kanji sheet with its scroll and focus on #strokes-door (verified: AFTER-EDGE {strokePage:false, sheet:true, active:'strokes-door', view:'reader'}). But that token is the only history integration in the app: with a 6-deep dictionary stack open (reader › 対戦 › 対 › 寸 › 待 › 9 strokes › 草 — reproduced), or inside a drift dive, or in review, history.back() leaves the site entirely (document unloads; verified: body[data-view] gone after back with no stroke room open). Nothing of the place survives return: storeEnvelope (corridor.js:920-941) persists srs/lists/readerPos but not view, stack, or passageId, so a fresh boot lands at the entry view. On iPhone — the app's explicit target, with an aria description in the stroke room telling users to 'use the browser or device Back command' — the edge-swipe is the habitual back gesture; one swipe from any sheet stack destroys a context the in-app backs restore perfectly (POP0-POP5 in the same run restored sheetScroll 120/150/300, reader scrollY 400, and focus to the originating token).
findings.repro: Serve corridor, open /?entry=shelf, open an article, long-press a content token -> 全項目, descend word -> kanji -> radical -> family kanji -> catalog -> kanji (6-deep crumb). Run history.back() (the edge-swipe equivalent): the document unloads instead of popping one sheet. Compare: open #strokes-door first, then history.back() -> only the stroke room closes.
findings.anchors: prototypes/corridor/corridor.js:2251-2272 (only openStrokePage pushes state), 2315-2322 (popstate handles only bunkiStrokeRoom), 920-941 (storeEnvelope: no view/stack/passage), 9889-9897 (stroke room tells users to use device Back)

findings.title: Every navigation and theme switch is a full render() DOM rebuild costing 100-201ms of main-thread block on desktop-class CPU — perceptible tap lag territory on the 390px target hardware
findings.evidence: PerformanceObserver longtask entries captured on every navigation across the whole walk show the same signature: each surface change or theme-stone tap produces one or more 100-200ms long tasks. Measured samples (headless Chromium, 390x844 mobile emulation, local http): shelf load 137ms+145ms; lessons open 123ms+170ms; kanji entry open from kanjidex 117ms and a 201ms peak (the only >200ms task in the modular build); minting a card + re-render 157-169ms; dojo open 123ms; and during the ten-stone palette cycle on a reader page, EVERY stone tap produced its own 106-158ms long task (10 taps → 10 sequential 100ms+ blocks: 110, 124, 122, 114, 122, 126, 106ms...), showing a theme change re-renders the entire tokenized article rather than just swapping the CSS custom-property theme that data-theme already drives. No task exceeded 201ms on this machine, but the corridor's stated target is a phone; a consistent 100-200ms desktop-class block is the classic 300-500ms mobile stall on the app's hottest paths (entry open, grade, theme tap). Anchor: render() at prototypes/corridor/corridor.js:11410 (full main rebuild), setKairoTheme at corridor.js:10743 followed by render() from the world picker.
findings.repro: 1) python3 -m http.server in prototypes/corridor; open index.html?entry=shelf in Chromium 390x844 with a PerformanceObserver({type:'longtask'}) armed. 2) Tap any shelf article → observe ~140ms long task. 3) Open the theme seal (top bar 藍) and tap each of the ten stones in sequence → observe one ~110-160ms long task per tap. 4) In 字引, select a part and open a kanji → observe up to 201ms. Harness: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Bunki-app/b3360808-e2ed-5db2-afd2-3ff21ea58fdf/scratchpad/walk5.js and walk1.js output.

findings.title: Standalone single-file build is 43.4MB and boots through a 287ms long task even on desktop-class CPU — multi-second parse/boot and memory pressure on a real phone
findings.evidence: prototypes/corridor/corridor-standalone.html is 43,415,666 bytes on this head (grew with the 30 re-landed articles, commit 49efa25). Serving it locally: load event at ~1.1s, then longtask entries of 109ms and 287ms during boot — the 287ms task is the largest single main-thread block measured anywhere in the app, from evaluating the embedded __CORRIDOR_BUNDLE__. JS heap right after boot: 33MB used / 85MB total. The modular index.html boots with nothing over 145ms. On mobile Safari the 43MB HTML string plus bundle eval will multiply into seconds of white paper and a large peak footprint; it also forecloses ever emailing/AirDropping the file casually. Not previously filed: triage P1-14 covered missing articles in this file, not its size/boot cost.
findings.repro: curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:8931/corridor-standalone.html (Content-Length 43415666); open it in Chromium with a buffered longtask observer → entries {109ms, 287ms} during boot. Harness: scratchpad/walk10.js, shot w10-standalone.png.
